QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_34

answer.text: Income retains its character when attributed to investors, who are taxed as if earning directly

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 254, 258), Category I and II Investment Funds enjoy pass-through status for non-business income. The income is taxed directly in the investors' hands as if they had invested directly, and it retains the same nature and proportion in their hands. The Trap: Pass-through does not mean double taxation, complete exemption, or no return at all. Investors must still report and pay tax on their share of the eligible income. Note: Business income of the fund is the exception — it is taxed at the fund level and exempt in the investors' hands, so pass-through applies only to non-business income.
